[LIMP.3.1.7] **A library that resolves but does not parse is reported
against the `import`.** When a search-path entry yields a file for the
requested identifier — [LIMP.3.1.2] having found one — and that file fails
to parse, the compiler must emit `DS_VALIDATE_LIBRARY_PARSE_FAILED` at the
**importing file's `import` line**, naming the library and carrying the
underlying parse failure in the message.

The location is the commitment here, and it is what an alternative
implementation could reasonably get differently. An author sees one pointer,
at a line in a file they wrote, instead of a position inside a library they
may not have written and cannot edit. The underlying failure is not
discarded — it travels in the message — but it does not become the
diagnostic's primary span, because a span into another file is not somewhere
the importing author can act.

This is the one resolution outcome distinct from [LIMP.3.1.2]'s: there, no
file answers to the identifier at all; here, one does and is not valid DS.
